mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals a consumption-led recession with a housing rebound, which depresses corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 12-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods meeting the trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for four consecutive months signals a broad-based contraction in economic activity, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods meeting the INDPRO trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 1% combined with a concurrent decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for two months signals a deflationary easing regime, which increases risk appetite and boosts S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% AND CPIAUCSL < 2% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods meeting the trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above the previous year's average while personal income (PAYEMS) grows below trend signals heightened precautionary savings, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > previous year average AND PAYEMS < previous year average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods meeting the trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods meeting the PAYEMS trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average while GDP growth (GDPC1) is flat or negative signals a housing-driven demand recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average AND GDPC1 <= previous quarter value for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods meeting the trigger condition.
